author: ValWood
body:
Dear all, 

The proposal has been made to obsolete GO:0000002 mitochondrial genome maintenance , and its regulation children, 
see  https://github.com/geneontology/go-ontology/issues/29646


Basically, this is a catch all term to describe phenotypic observations for multiple processes (including transport/lipid metabolism/ DNA metabolism/ fission/ fusion etc)

Experimental annotations that need to be reviewed are here: 
https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17sfikFTQoFAKtV9jbH9k2JlPsH3EdKXj5NmX32UegNg/edit?gid=0#gid=0

author: deustp01
body: I'm confused. Although Reactome is tagged as having [four usages of GO:0000002](https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/d/17sfikFTQoFAKtV9jbH9k2JlPsH3EdKXj5NmX32UegNg/edit?gid=0#gid=0), in fact none of the Reactome instances in the spreadsheet use that term. They all use a grandchild, GO:0006264 "mitochondrial DNA replication" which, as far as I can tell remains a legitimate GO BP term.

author: jlewsmith
body:
I think I'm confused as well. I was assuming we could keep the term with the new name of "mitochondrial genome organization," but in truth it's no longer accurate for cases where a mutant shows loss of mitochondrial DNA. In that case, "maintenance" is more accurate than "organization."  For example, PMID 30240789.

Would GO:0000001 mitochondrion inheritance be the alternative choice here?

author: pgaudet
body: @ValWood you need to re-run the query with 'direct annotations only'.

author: ValWood
body:
Ah it is. I didn't realise (or had forgotten) that these propagate.  There are only 80 reannotation to do.
I don't know how to restrict to direct terms, for the spreadsheet, so I will relocte the descendants and then  rerun the query.
Once that is done I'll update the spreadsheet.

author: ValWood
body:
replacement ticket is here:

https://github.com/geneontology/go-annotation/issues/5767

@jlewsmith  looking at  PMID 30240789  "loss of mitochondrial DNA" is a phenotype. This phenotype is a consequence of lots of processes. In this case, like;y a problem with fission or fusion (which the subject mgm1, a mitochondrial dynamin family fusion GTPase, is involved in. I haven't read the paper but  if you can't  get fission or fusion, you could do GO:0007005 
mitochondrion organization.
You can only really capture "loss of mitochondrial DNA" precisely if you have a phenotype ontology.

author: jlewsmith
body: Thank you @ValWood - that's quite helpful. I'll look again for the right fit.
